name: Tool and Context Poisoning
description: Adversarial content in tool definitions, descriptions, schemas, results, or protocol metadata (e.g. MCP servers) that manipulates an agent's tool selection, parameters, or subsequent reasoning.
differs: Distinguished from generic Indirect Prompt Injection (T1.002) by the surface: the payload lives in the *tool/protocol layer* (descriptions, schemas, results, provenance) rather than in user-facing content. Detection relies on tool-metadata diffing and provenance checks.
